children: Organon reported that a VA system-wide switch from HUMIRA to HADLIMA had a 1.3% switchback rate over 12 months. Adherence remained similar, and average per-patient pharmacy costs fell by $8,100 in the first year; no prior-period cost comparison was provided.
VA switchback rate was 1.3% over 12 months
The low rate supports persistence after the formulary switch, though the release cites published switchback rates of 16–18%.
First-year pharmacy costs fell $8,100 per patient
The reported savings could support biosimilar adoption; no prior-period cost comparison was provided.
Adherence remained similar pre- and post-switch
Similar adherence suggests the transition did not reduce adherence in the analyzed VA population.
VA selected HADLIMA for its national formulary in 2024
The study evaluates an existing formulary decision, rather than announcing a new customer or contract.

This is real-world evidence on a VA formulary transition already implemented in 2024, rather than a new commercial agreement. Broader catalyst potential would require evidence of adoption beyond the VA or quantified effects on Organon's revenue or margins.
